verdict.probe_answer: Both arms: yes to all three. Both diagnose the gawk 'load' reserved-builtin collision correctly (the -v load="$LOAD" assignment in the NORMALIZED awk call), both fixes are minimal one-line renames confined solely to scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh (Arm A -> load_avg, Arm B -> loadavg), and neither diff touches test/hooks.js or any other file. No other awk -v invocation in the shown context uses 'load' as a bare variable name (the other calls use $1 positionally or already-distinct names like best_load/normalized), so both fixes fully address the reported failure with no residual occurrences.
verdict.rationale: Functionally identical fixes: both rename the offending awk variable away from the reserved word 'load', both are single-line, single-file changes, and both leave hooks.js and all other code untouched, directly resolving the reported CI failure. The only difference is stylistic: Arm B adds a one-line comment explaining that 'load' is a gawk reserved word, which is a legitimate 'why' comment guarding against a future regression, while Arm A has no comment and picks a different but equally valid replacement name (load_avg vs loadavg). This is a minor documentation nicety, not a correctness, completeness, or scope difference, so it does not rise to material superiority for either arm. Neither arm added or touched tests. Parity.
